title: Microeconomics
tagline: Preferences and utility, consumer demand, income and substitution effects, choice under uncertainty, production and cost, competitive and general equilibrium, and welfare
summary: Microeconomics studies how households and firms make choices and how those choices interact in markets. This course develops the theory of the consumer — preferences, utility, demand, the measurement of welfare and choice under uncertainty — and of the firm — technology, cost and supply — and then combines them in competitive and general equilibrium, asking when markets allocate resources efficiently and when they fail.

chapters.title: Preferences and utility
chapters.summary: Budget sets, preference relations, indifference curves, the marginal rate of substitution and utility functions that represent preferences.

chapters.title: Consumer choice and demand
chapters.summary: Utility maximisation, Marshallian demand, the indirect utility function and Roy’s identity.

chapters.title: Income and substitution effects
chapters.summary: Expenditure minimisation, Hicksian demand, the Slutsky equation, and measuring welfare changes with compensating and equivalent variation.

chapters.title: Endowments, labour supply and saving
chapters.summary: Choice with endowments, the trade-off between labour and leisure, and consumption over time with borrowing and lending.

chapters.title: Choice under uncertainty
chapters.summary: Lotteries, expected utility, risk aversion, certainty equivalents and the demand for insurance.

chapters.title: Production and cost
chapters.summary: Technology and production functions, returns to scale, cost minimisation and cost curves in the short and long run.

chapters.title: Profit maximisation and competitive markets
chapters.summary: Firm and industry supply, and short- and long-run equilibrium in perfectly competitive markets.

chapters.title: General equilibrium and exchange
chapters.summary: The Edgeworth box, Walrasian equilibrium and its existence, and general equilibrium with production.

chapters.title: Efficiency, welfare and market failure
chapters.summary: Pareto efficiency, the two welfare theorems, social welfare functions, and how externalities and public goods break the first welfare theorem.
